caption:
How much does it actually cost to visit Yellowstone + Grand Teton? 👀🏔️

We broke down every major cost so you can actually plan this trip flights, hotels, rental cars, food, gas, and park entrance fees for Yellowstone National Park and Grand Teton National Park.

For a 4–5 day trip, a realistic budget is around $1,300–$1,600 per person, depending on your travel dates, which gateway town you stay in (Jackson, West Yellowstone, or Gardiner), and how early you book flights.

Here’s where the money goes on a Yellowstone and Grand Teton road trip:
✈️ Flights: biggest variable fly into Jackson Hole or Bozeman and compare both
🏨 Hotels: book 6+ months out for summer, prices spike in June- August
🚗 Rental car: non-negotiable, the parks are huge and there’s no real transit
⛽ Gas: you’ll drive hundreds of miles between geyser basins, Old Faithful, Grand Prismatic, Jenny Lake, and Mormon Row
🎟️ Park pass: one America the Beautiful pass covers both parks for a full year

Pro tip: visiting in shoulder season (May or September) can cut your Yellowstone trip cost significantly, fewer crowds, cheaper lodging, and the wildlife is unreal.

This is the most scenic drive in South Dakota and almost no one talks about it 👇

Needles Highway is a 14 mile drive inside Custer State Park, South Dakota that winds through granite spires, one-lane rock tunnels, and hairpin turns.

It’s in the Black Hills between Custer and Mt Rushmore and it’s one of the best road trips in the USA if you love dramatic landscapes.

📍 SAVE THIS FOR YOUR BLACK HILLS TRIP:
Must stop along the drive:
Needles Eye Tunnel - one lane tunnel carved through granite
Cathedral Spires Overlook - best photo spot
Sylvan Lake for hiking & picnics
Hike if you have time:
Cathedral Spires Trail, 1.6 miles out & back to the base of granite walls
Sunday Gulch Trail, 3.9 mile loop from Sylvan Lake with ladders + scrambles
Little Devil’s Tower Trail, 3.8 miles with views of Black Elk Peak

Best time to go: Summer to early fall. Go early morning or late afternoon, less traffic, better light. Winter = road closures.

Pro tip: Drive slow, road is VERY narrow. Vehicles over 8ft wide / 12ft tall won’t fit through tunnels. Pair it with Wildlife Loop Road in Custer State Park.

Rialto Beach in Olympic National Park feels like stepping into a moody coastal movie, towering sea stacks, massive driftwood, crashing Pacific waves and rugged Washington coastline in every direction.

🌊 Check the tide schedule before hiking
🥾 Wear waterproof shoes with good grip
📸 Visit early morning or around sunset for dreamy light
🌧️ Bring a rain jacket, the weather changes quickly
🪵 Never turn your back on the ocean or climb unstable driftwood

Olympic National Park is one of the most diverse national parks in the USA, where you can hike through an ancient temperate rainforest, explore dramatic Pacific Northwest beaches, chase waterfalls, and stand among mountain peaks, all in one trip.

🥾 Best hikes and places to visit in Olympic National Park:

🌿 Hoh Rain Forest
• Hall of Mosses Trail :0.8-mile loop
• Spruce Nature Trail : 1.2-mile loop
Walk beneath moss covered trees in one of the most magical rainforests in Washington State.

🏔️ Hurricane Ridge
• Hurricane Hill Trail : 3.4 miles round trip
One of the best Olympic National Park hikes for panoramic mountain views, wildflowers, and possible wildlife sightings.

🌊 Rialto Beach
• Hole in the Wall Trail : around 3.3 miles round trip
Explore sea stacks, driftwood-covered shores, tide pools, and one of the most beautiful beaches on the Olympic Peninsula. Check the tide chart before hiking!

💧 Sol Duc Valley
• Sol Duc Falls Trail : 1.6 miles round trip
A short forest hike leading to one of the most iconic waterfalls in Olympic National Park.

💙 Lake Crescent
• Marymere Falls Trail : 1.8 miles round trip
• Mount Storm King : around 4 miles round trip, steep and challenging
Stop for the crystal clear lake views, then choose between a peaceful waterfall hike or an adventurous climb.
